cluster_name: DR Congo Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak hits 3,874 cases, health workers strike
event_summary: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo reached 3,874 confirmed cases and 1,751 deaths by August 6, becoming the country's largest-ever outbreak. WHO Director-General Tedros visited Kinshasa on August 5-6 urging emergency scale-up while health workers at the Ituri epicentre struck over unpaid wages.
tldr: The most operationally damaging development in this cluster is an institutional failure inside the crisis: nurses and caregivers at the Ituri epicentre walked off the job over unpaid wages, leaving treatment centres understaffed even as WHO declared the response was being outpaced. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or treatment, leaving authorities racing without a biomedical backstop — a fact noted almost exclusively by Canadian coverage, which adds Health Canada's clearance of a Moderna Bundibugyo trial as the first countermeasure signal. A passenger boat was intercepted on the Congo River before reaching Kinshasa on August 5, flagging active spread risk to the 17-million-person capital. French-language outlets (RFI Afrique, AFP/France 24 FR) carry the containment-geographic angle most specifically, while Anglophone wire services and Asian outlets cluster around the WHO call-for-support frame.

bottom_line: DR Congo's Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak is now the country's largest ever, with 3,874 cases and 1,751 deaths in 14 weeks, and the response is being compounded by a second crisis: health workers at the Ituri epicentre are striking over unpaid wages, abandoning treatment centres mid-outbreak. Thirteen-country coverage converges on WHO's emergency call while almost entirely overlooking the absence of any approved vaccine or treatment for this strain, an angle surfaced only by Canada's Globe and Mail alongside news of a Moderna trial clearance.
